subject: WebSocket idle resets + 504 spike (FinNova) - customer escalates
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@finnova.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinNova SRE <sre@finnova.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2027 08:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: production: intermittent WS timeouts and 504 spikes (urgent)

Monica —

We started seeing a burst of websocket timeouts and streaming hangs this morning (~08:45 PT) across multiple customers of our product; FinNova is one of the affected tenants. Symptoms: streaming responses stop emitting chunks for ~10–30s, client-side websocket connections drop with 1006/timeout errors, and our edge shows a corresponding 504 spike.

Affected routes/IDs:
- /v1/run/chat (model: redwood/gptx-11b)
- Sample traces: trace=4b7f3a1e, trace=4b7f3f2b, trace=4b7f3ffd

This started around 08:45 and we've had ~120 failed requests and a 5.3% error rate in the last 30 minutes (compared to normal <0.1%). We rely on streaming for our real-time UI — this is impacting a live demo scheduled for leadership at 10:30 PT.

Attached: finnova-client-traces.txt (snippets from our client side including websocket client logs and trace ids). Please escalate.

Thanks,
Samir
SRE, FinNova

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2027 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: production: intermittent WS timeouts and 504 spikes (urgent)

Monica / Connor — quick triage: I've pulled the traces Samir sent and cross-referenced them with the runtime logs. Observations:

- Pattern: long pauses in chunked output where the runtime returns 0 bytes for 12–28s before resuming; client then times out and reconnects.
- Autoscaler: no new instances added between 08:40 and 09:10 on the affected pool; there were sustained inflight requests but not enough CPU signal due to a stall in the KV cache refill path.
- Kernel/version note: two nodes in the pool are on an older inference kernel (1.8.3) while the majority are on 1.9.x. The older kernel path shows a known micro-deadlock in our attention kernel that can cause per-sequence stalls under specific batch reordering.

Immediate mitigation we recommend (low-risk, can be applied in minutes):
1) Reroute FinNova traffic away from the two 1.8.3 nodes (force drain + soft redirect).
2) Trigger a manual +30% capacity bump in the dedicated pool for the next 2 hours to reduce queueing/backpressure.
3) Toggle prefix-KV bypass for the affected model variant to avoid the refill path while we patch.

I'll attach triage notes with commands and log snippets: triage-notes-20270522.md

Connor — can you own the drain + routing change? Monica — please confirm with the customer before we change routing.

-Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: FINOVA exec brief: streaming idle-resets and 504 spike (10:30 PT briefing)

Evelyn / Hannah — putting an exec-ready note in the thread for the 10:30 briefing and to request leadership support for credits & priority. I will be on the call with FinNova.

Executive summary (2–3 bullets):
- What happened: between 08:45–09:30 PT on 2027-05-22 we observed intermittent chunked/websocket output stalls on requests to redwood/gptx-11b serving FinNova. Client websocket connections experienced idle timeouts leading to a spike in 504s and a customer-visible error rate increase up to 5.3% at peak.
- Scope & impact: FinNova reported ~120 failed streams and saw degraded demo behavior for critical accounts; this impacts their leadership demo scheduled during the incident. Potential SLA exposure: increased error rate and latency for their paid seats.
- Root cause (initial): a kernel behavior on a subset of backend nodes (inference kernel 1.8.3) that can enter a micro-deadlock during particular batch reorder patterns, causing KV cache refill stalls and prolonged output silence.

Immediate actions completed:
- Rohan identified the kernel mismatch and recommended routing/drain.
- Connor executed a soft drain of the two affected hosts and we temporarily routed traffic to healthy nodes.
- We requested +30% capacity and toggled prefix-KV bypass for the model variant.

Customer asks:
- FinNova requested an estimated stabilization window and an executive note for their leadership; they also asked for a credit given the demo impact.

Requested leadership actions:
- Approve a one-time customer credit (recommended 10% of last month’s inference spend) and expedited SRM patch backport to the two affected nodes.
- Approve an SRE war room for full remediation and postmortem (Connor to lead).

Attachments: exec-brief-ws-504.pdf (attached here for distribution)

Next steps — owner assignments:
- Customer comms draft + credit approval: Evelyn (owner)
- War room + postmortem: Connor (owner)
- Patch backport schedule: Rohan + infra kernel team

I will follow up with the customer after leadership confirmation.

—Monica
